name: Nodular Lymphocyte Predominant Hodgkin Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of large lymphocyte predominant (LP) cells with 'popcorn' nuclei in a nodular growth pattern
LP cells positive for CD20, CD45, and negative for CD15 and CD30
Localized lymphadenopathy without systemic B symptoms
Exclusion of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and other lymphomas by histopathology and immunophenotyping

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological identification of LP cells with characteristic immunophenotype and nodular pattern, excluding classical Hodgkin lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires excisional lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry

occasional.symptomName: Abnormality of bone marrow cell morphology

laboratory: Absence of CD15 and CD30 expression on LP cells
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing localized lymphadenopathy
Absence of widespread nodal or extranodal disease
genetic: No specific recurrent genetic mutations identified; clonal B-cell population demonstrated by molecular studies
other: Histopathology showing nodular pattern with LP cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD45, BCL6

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse or follicular growth pattern without LP cells

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Extranodal disease or bone marrow involvement
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Orphanet: Nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. ORPHA:86893.
Vassilakopoulos TP, Pangalis GA. Nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma: a distinct clinical entity. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2018.
